content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name]. My system uses 12V DC. I've selected a [product_name] controller ([article_no]) which supports 12 to 24V DC. I need two 4-20mA outputs, so I added an [product_name] output module ([article_no]). Can I use the output module with the same 12V power? Its datasheet mentions 24V, but I'd prefer not to add another power supply.
No, it's not possible to run it on 12V directly. You could consider using a voltage doubler to convert 12V DC to 24V DC.
I'm referring to a voltage doubler circuit for this purpose.
Thanks for the clarification. That's disappointing.

analysis.insight_summary: The user learns that the [product_name] expansion module (for analog output) requires 24V DC and cannot operate on 12V DC, unlike the main controller. This creates a challenge for integration in low-voltage setups, leading to user frustration and a need for either an external power supply or voltage conversion to meet the requirements documented in official datasheets.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for all modules in their setup to efficiently operate from a single 12V power source, without needing extra power supplies or voltage converters.
